title: Localized Dynamics-Aware Domain Adaptation for Off-Dynamics Offline Reinforcement Learning
claim: Cluster target and source transitions, estimate per-cluster dynamics gaps with classifiers, then filter source data for offline RL.
layout: Single row, left-to-right, two stacked input rows merging into one flow
description: A left-to-right flow diagram. At far left, two stacked rows show a cyan target dataset (D_tar) and a green source dataset (D_src) as cylinders. Each feeds a small table of (s, a, s') columns, with the s' column outlined in red. The target row goes through 'clustering' into a rounded box of four red ellipses numbered 1 to 4, holding cyan points. The source row goes through 'assignment' into a similar box that mixes green and cyan points, labeled D_src ∪ D_tar. A vertical arrow links the two boxes. The merged box feeds 'train cluster-wise classifier', which produces per-cluster KL estimates D_1(s,a) ⇒ D̂¹_KL through D_4(s,a) ⇒ D̂⁴_KL, with vertical dots between them. Next, 'filtering' leads to a reduced cluster box, and from there an arrow leads to an 'Offline RL' box. A 'dataset regularization' arrow loops over the top into the Offline RL box. Cyan and green separate target from source, and red ellipses mark clusters.
caption: An overview of our proposed framework. We first perform K-means clustering on the next state for the target dataset and then assign source transitions to clusters via their next state. We estimate the local KL divergence between source and target dynamics in each cluster using cluster-wise classifiers, and selectively retain source transitions for downstream offline RL algorithms. We further introduce a dataset regularization term to ensure policy consistency with the target dataset.
abstract: Off-dynamics offline reinforcement learning (RL) aims to learn a policy for a target domain using limited target data and abundant source data collected under different transition dynamics. Existing methods typically address dynamics mismatch either globally over the state space or via pointwise data filtering; these approaches can miss localized cross-domain similarities or incur high computational cost. We propose Localized Dynamics-Aware Domain Adaptation (LoDADA), which exploits localized dynamics mismatch to better reuse source data. LoDADA clusters transitions from source and target datasets and estimates cluster-level dynamics discrepancy via domain discrimination. Source transitions from clusters with small discrepancy are more likely to be retained compared with those from clusters with large discrepancy. This yields a fine-grained and scalable data selection strategy that avoids overly coarse global assumptions and expensive per-sample filtering. We provide theoretical insights and extensive experiments across environments with diverse global and local dynamics shifts. Results show that LoDADA consistently outperforms state-of-the-art off-dynamics offline RL methods by better leveraging localized distribution mismatch.
